requirements.requirement: On node1, new user passwords must be enforced to require a minimum length of 12 characters
requirements.summary: A pwquality.conf.d drop-in (90-complexity.conf) sets minlen=12, confirmed present both pre- and post-reboot, and a real non-root user's passwd attempt with a short (7-char) password was rejected (exit 10) while pwscore independently confirmed rejection of sub-12-character passwords and acceptance of a 12+ character compliant password.

requirements.requirement: On node1, new user passwords must be enforced to use at least 3 different character classes
requirements.summary: The same drop-in sets minclass=3, confirmed present pre- and post-reboot; pwscore rejected all-lowercase and low-class passwords, and real non-root users had low-class passwords rejected (exit 10) while a 3-class compliant password was accepted (exit 0), repeated after reboot with a fresh test user.

requirements.requirement: Policy is actually wired into PAM so it applies to real password changes, not just a config file
requirements.summary: pam_pwquality.so was confirmed already required in system-auth and password-auth before and after the change, and end-to-end enforcement was demonstrated with real non-root passwd invocations rejecting weak passwords and accepting compliant ones, both before and after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Configuration change does not conflict with or duplicate existing pwquality settings
requirements.summary: Base /etc/security/pwquality.conf was left with only commented-out defaults; a grep for active minlen/minclass lines in the base file returned no matches, showing the new settings live only in the clean drop-in with no duplication.

requirements.requirement: Policy configuration and enforcement persist across a service-affecting event (here, a reboot)
requirements.summary: A pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id, policy file contents, PAM wiring) was captured, the node was rebooted (acknowledged immediately, then went unreachable during the transition), came back with a different boot_id, and both the drop-in file contents and PAM wiring were re-verified afterward, with a fresh real-user passwd test again confirming enforcement.

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented and verified a 12-character/3-class password complexity policy on node1 via a clean pwquality.conf.d drop-in, with PAM wiring already in place, and demonstrated real end-to-end enforcement (rejection of non-compliant and acceptance of compliant passwords by an actual non-root user) both before and after a genuine reboot that changed the node's boot identity, confirming persistence. All test accounts created for verification were removed afterward, and the only minor hygiene note is a redundant early passwd invocation (immediately overwritten) and a small leftover reboot log file, neither of which affected the final system state.
limitations: The pre-restart baseline command (cmd-10ef2e7fbd184845) used a malformed grep invocation ('-H minlen -H minclass') that errored on 'minclass' and only partially displayed the file; the actual full file contents were independently confirmed moments earlier (cmd-bf67417bade84d72) and again post-reboot (cmd-3a4b4eabc8534c99), so this is a cosmetic command-syntax issue rather than evidence of a missing setting.

Root's own password enforcement was not tested (root is exempt from pwquality by default unless enforce_for_root is set), but the task only concerns 'new user passwords' generally and non-root real-user testing directly demonstrates the required behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing actions map cleanly to the task: creating the pwquality.conf.d drop-in (retained, intended change), creating/cleaning up two disposable test users (complextest, posttest) used solely to prove enforcement, and the reboot used for the restart-evidence protocol. Both test users were fully removed via pkill+userdel -r (cmd-6d9aa438026e4429, cmd-92cc323b952d459a) with no residual accounts or home directories. One minor unnecessary mutation: cmd-d45ffb583ab047b4 set an initial weak password for complextest via root passwd (which bypasses pwquality since root is exempt) and was immediately superseded by cmd-639d7772e7674ad5's chpasswd call moments later, making the first invocation redundant; it left no lasting residue since the account was later deleted. The reboot process left a small /tmp/reboot.log file as a side effect of the backgrounded reboot command, visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; this is low-risk, bounded log residue directly tied to the restart-evidence action rather than an abandoned artifact. No failed services, no unsafe socket exposure changes (listening sockets are unchanged sshd/chronyd, differing only by PID across the reboot), and package health reported clean before and after.
